draft.title: Judges and magistrates in criminal cases
card: In a criminal case, the judge or magistrate acts as an impartial umpire. They manage the hearing and make sure it runs fairly and follows the rules.
They decide questions of law, such as whether a piece of evidence can be used. In a jury trial, they also direct the jury on the law it must apply.
If the accused is found guilty or pleads guilty, the judge or magistrate passes sentence.
The parties, the prosecution and the defence, present their own cases. The judge or magistrate does not run either side's case.
draft.remember: The judge or magistrate manages, rules on law and sentences. The parties argue their cases.

a.q: Which task is done by the judge in a criminal jury trial?
opts: Explaining to the jury the law it must apply
Calling the witnesses for the prosecution
Planning the defence for the accused
Deciding the facts and giving the verdict
a.why: The judge directs the jury on the law. The prosecution calls its own witnesses and the defence plans its own case, as the parties present their cases. Deciding the facts and giving the verdict is the jury's job, so it is not the judge's task here.
a.clue: The judge is an umpire, not one of the parties.

b.q: In a County Court trial, the defence asks to use a document, and the prosecution objects. Who decides whether it can be used?
opts: The judge, as it is a question of law
The jury, as it decides all disputes
The prosecution, as it made the objection
The defence, as it asked to use the document
b.why: Whether evidence can be used is a question of law, which the judge decides. The jury is not the one to rule on it. The parties argue their sides, but neither one decides the issue.
b.clue: Ruling on whether evidence is allowed is a question of law.

a.best: Explaining to the jury the law it must apply

b.best: The judge, as it is a question of law

problems.detail: The clue says ruling on evidence is 'a question of law', and only the right option ends 'as it is a question of law'. A student can match the phrase without knowing who decides.
